title: The Double Charge
subtitle: A mobile retry creates a second payment

brief.narrative: The client times out after the server commits, then retries POST /payments. The server treats the retry as a new command.
symptoms: Payment API metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: At-least-once delivery replayed a record whose side effect was already committed.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Processing exceeded the poll interval and triggered repeated consumer-group rebalances.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: A single hot key concentrated traffic on one partition.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: The create operation lacked a stable idempotency key and replayed a committed side effect.
options.feedback: Correct. Idempotency needs a key scope, retention window, concurrent-request behavior, and an atomic relationship with the side effect.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Reduce/bound processing, tune poll records and interval from measured worst cases, use cooperative rebalancing, and isolate poison or slow records.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Use near-cache/request coalescing, replicate or split the hot value when safe, protect origin with limits, and track per-key/per-shard load.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Require a scoped idempotency key, atomically store request hash and result, return the original result on replay, and reject key reuse with different input.
options.feedback: Correct. Idempotency needs a key scope, retention window, concurrent-request behavior, and an atomic relationship with the side effect.

options.text: Use an idempotency/inbox key in the same transaction as the side effect, then commit offsets; choose Kafka transactions only when their boundary fits.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.
